headline: The 2026 data outgrow CDLZ's flat model at the frontier: the minimal revision is a bunching model whose labor-demand elasticity DECLINES with bite past a threshold near Kaitz ~0.50 / bite ~0.094 - mild-monopsony-positive below, competitive-negative above - which reproduces the paper era and resolves the 2016-2019 episode the flat model misses by 3.2 sigma (though no cohort's job loss is yet statistically significant).

figures.caption: A: recalibrated employment-effect-by-Kaitz function, paper-era events (blue) vs all events through 2024 (orange), with the CDLZ flat model and the updated monopsony-exhaustion threshold (K*~0.50) plus a +-1 slope-SE fan. B: cohort-level employment-by-bite view - W4/W5 share Kaitz but differ in bite, and the bite threshold (0.094) reconciles the 2016-2019 miss the flat model makes by ~2.8-3.2 sigma.
figures.alt: Two panels. Left: net employment percent vs Kaitz index with noisy binned point estimates straddling zero, a flat dashed reference line near +3%, and a solid threshold curve flat until Kaitz 0.49 then declining inside a wide shaded uncertainty fan. Right: five labeled cohort points vs bite; W4 2016-2019 sits at -4% far below the flat +2.8% line while the threshold model bends down past bite 0.094 to meet it.

notes: Nothing is statistically significant: the flat model is not rejected, only its central prediction at the post-frontier cohort (W4, t=-1.7). The update is an honest central-tendency shift.

Threshold parameters are [CALIBRATED] to moments 001/002 already produced (window bite-slope zero-crossing/slope), not from a new in-session structural estimation (permitted by brief item 6). Slope SE is large (t=-1.7): threshold LOCATION is better identified than its magnitude.
Bite - not Kaitz alone - is the operative state variable: W4 and W5 have near-identical Kaitz (0.513 vs 0.520) but opposite effects driven by bite (0.116 vs 0.094).

Compute this session: three Kaitz-binned joint TWFE regressions (the step follow-up 002 was killed on), reusing 001's validated panel/machinery; no microdata re-fetched. Read results/theory_update.md for the full 'Theory, updated to 2026' section.
